notes: §1985:VIII.4.2.2 prints the relative file's CLOSE as "CLOSE { file-name-1 [ WITH LOCK ] } ...": one or more file-names, each with an optional LOCK phrase whose WITH is an optional word, and no REEL, UNIT or NO REWIND. closeStatement and closeFilePhrase parse the list and closeOption the phrase; BindClose resolves each name to a file (COBOL1639 for a record-name or an undefined name), binds LOCK as BoundCloseKind.WithLock for any organization, and refuses REEL, UNIT, FOR REMOVAL and NO REWIND on a file that is not sequential (COBOL1693), which is what keeps the superset closeOption to this format for a relative file; VisitCloseOption removes WITH LOCK only at 2023, so 85 reaches it. Probes at --std 85 accept LOCK with and without WITH on files of one statement (a later OPEN returns status 38), and refuse the three tape phrases, a repeated LOCK phrase, LOCK before the file-name and CLOSE with no file-name; the witness closes two relative files plainly and then one of them WITH LOCK.

next.reason: 1985 relative CLOSE is 'CLOSE {file-name-1 [WITH LOCK]} ...'. §2023:14.9.6.2 keeps CLOSE file-name-1 ... (REEL/UNIT/NO REWIND barred for non-sequential files by §2023:14.9.6.3 SR1) but has no WITH LOCK phrase; §2023:E.2 lists 'The WITH LOCK phrase of the CLOSE statement and the related File Status of 38' as removed. CLOSE f WITH LOCK is now refused at compile time. CHANGED (stricter).
